<role>
you are a principal motion designer and real-time graphics engineer. you make product launch films entirely in three.js, every frame code, to the standard of the brand's own films. you prove quality with measurements and independent critics, not adjectives.
</role>

<brief>
- the product, and the 3-5 facts the film may state (verbatim, nothing invented)
- the reference film to beat
- length, aspect and resolution
- never show: [logos, people, footage you don't own]
</brief>

<study>
read the reference frame by frame and turn it into numbers: cut rhythm, camera speeds, the hero motion curve, type size and timing, stage colour. those numbers are the bar. measure it, never copy it.
</study>

<build>
- storyboard first: one table of time, shot, what it proves and the cut out. 2-3 s per shot, and frame 0 is already the money shot
- one seek clock: every pixel is a pure function of time
- build every element (the device, its screen ui, each shot, the type) alone in its own lab before it joins the film
- the screen ui is code, the type is drawn on canvas, and every threshold is a crossfade (hard ones flash for a frame)
</build>

<loop>
- builder and critic are always separate agents. the critic starts fresh every round, judges the rendered frames against the reference, scores them and names the single biggest gap. the builder fixes only that
- blind test: mix your frames with the reference's. if a judge can tell which is which, it isn't done
- wow gate: split the film into 3 s windows. every one must be a yes
</loop>

<sound>
- one real track, lined up so its own final hit lands on the end card and played as one continuous piece. cut on its beat
- a clean, real sound on every small move, with the hero moments clearly audible
- music quiet (about -34 lufs), and always a music-only version
</sound>

<qa>
render at 60fps and measure frozen frames, one-frame pops, black frames and loudness. then watch it like the client would: empty space, text over text, labels that lie, shots that linger.
</qa>

Three.jsでピストンとクランクが動く立体図解、1行の依頼から夜のあいだにClaude Code（Opus 5.5）に作らせてみた。作業時間は8分。

■ 作ったもの
・ピストン、コンロッド、クランク（主軸・腕・ピン・はずみ車）、透けるシリンダー、ヘッド、点火プラグ、燃焼室の炎
・Remotionで1080×1920・30fpsの縦長、32秒の動画
・画像素材は1枚も使ってない。部品も炎も全部コードで描いてる

■ どう動いてるか
・ピストンの高さとコンロッドの傾きは、クランクの角度から式で毎コマ計算してる
・4ストロークなので720°に1回、上死点の直後だけ燃焼室が光る
・部品のラベルの線は、3Dの点を同じカメラで画面に投影して引いてる。だからぐるっと回しても寄っても、線がちゃんと部品を指したまま

■ 作り方（3ステップ）
1. 依頼は「Three.jsでピストンとクランクの動きを回転・拡大できる立体図解にする」の1行だけ
2. もともと入ってた@remotion/threeと@react-three/fiberだけで組ませる。追加のインストールはなし
3. 途中の静止画を3回見て、ピストンリングの向き・カメラの距離と高さ・ラベルとグラフの重なりを直してから書き出し。ヘッドレスのレンダー（--gl=angle）でも立体はそのまま出て、書き出しは1回で済んだ

■ 注意点
・元の投稿のスキル「Anatomy」は入れてないし、試してもいない。手元のThree.jsで組んだだけ
・炎は半透明の光る円柱と点光源。元の投稿みたいなWebGLシェーダーの炎・水・プラズマはやってない
・クランクの釣り合いのおもりは形を簡単にしてて、角度によっては暗い板っぽく見えるコマがある
・見る人が自分で回したり拡大したりはできない。動画の中でカメラを動かして見せてるだけ

How to make a short AI dialogue cartoon with Claude Code or Codex:

You need:
- An ElevenLabs API key with Text to Speech + Voices: Read
- An OpenAI key (gpt-image) for the art
- Optional: an OpenRouter key so Gemini can listen to and check the audio
- ffmpeg, Node, Python, Chrome

Save your keys in files (e.g. ~/.config/elevenlabs/api-key), open Claude Code or Codex in an empty folder (in Codex, allow network access), and paste:

Make me one ~30 second animated dialogue video (1920x1080 MP4).

Characters: [your choice]
Situation: [your choice]
Art style: [your choice]

Write a funny 6-8 line back-and-forth with a punchline. Keys are in ~/.config/*/api-key; never print them.

1. Voices: search the ElevenLabs voice library, audition 3-4 voices per character on a real line, and have Gemini (via OpenRouter) pick the best fit.
2. Speech: eleven_v3 with-timestamps, one request per line, with an acting tag like [exasperated]. Use curl.
3. Audio: trim lines using both the timestamps and the waveform (so nothing is clipped and there's no dead air), fit to 30s, add quiet ambience, and compute a per-frame loudness envelope per character.
4. Art: one 16:9 scene with both characters facing each other, mouths closed. Then one edit per character: "change ONLY their mouth to open mid-word."
5. Mouths: diff each edit against the scene to cut out a feathered mouth overlay.
6. Render: canvas page + Puppeteer + ffmpeg. Show a mouth overlay when that character is loud. Word-synced captions styled to match the art. One fixed shot, both characters always visible, no camera moves, and no black first frame.
7. QA: have Gemini check the audio against the script, fix issues, and check test stills before the full render.

Keep all working files in a source/ folder so it can be re-rendered later.
